title: fix(lint): ADR-0087's prescription detector reads a rewrite whose TO side is an instruction
body:
Fixes #18745

ADR-0087's `no-migration-prescription` detector missed a framed FROM → TO line again, so
an exemption the categories inherit can be held by SILENCE rather than by a finding. This
adds the one arm that was missing, answers the three questions the claim could not, and
hands back the one reading that is not this PR's to act on.

This is ⛔ NOT a defect in PR #18736. That PR's exemption rests on four positively
verified predicates and the gate printed `-- verified`. What recurred is the INSTRUMENT.

Clause-②: no — one repo gate script, no published byte moves (measured below).

## Q1 — which spelling was missed, beside the branch that should have caught it

Anchored on SYMBOLS and reported where they actually are. In
`scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`: `findMigrationPrescription` is at **:1562** on
`origin/main` and at **:1685** on this branch. The card's `:204-214` for the header
paragraph is NOT stale — `That argument is correct and it was accepted` really does open
at **:204** on `origin/main`, and still does here (this PR appends its cross-reference
after that paragraph rather than editing it).

```
MISSED:  **Migration — `api: { … }` → delete the property.**        .changeset/18318-evalcontext-no-query-api.md
BRANCH:  2, `framed-line`  (REWRITE_RE under MIGRATION_FRAMING_RE)
```

Predicate by predicate on that one line, each with its own non-zero control:

| predicate | on the missed line | non-zero control |
|---|---|---|
| `MIGRATION_FRAMING_RE` | `true` | `false` on `plain prose` |
| FROM side is an `OPERAND` | `true` (a backticked span) | — |
| an `ARROW` is present | `true` | — |
| `REWRITE_RE` (needs an `OPERAND` on BOTH sides) | **`false`** | `true` on the same line with `` `os.exists` `` as the TO side |

So it failed on exactly ONE predicate. `delete the property` is an INSTRUCTION, not a
name — and `OPERAND` is a backticked code span or a dotted/slashed identifier path. A
removal has no new name to put on the right, so the most careful prescription an author
can write for one is invisible to every arm.

## Q2 — the #8277 miss in the gate's header is a DIFFERENT hole

Measured on `fc71b84:.changeset/lucky-schools-smash.md` through the exported detector.

| | #8277 (the header's case) | #18745 (this round) |
|---|---|---|
| the prescription | `read` `` `result.driverFault?.message` `` `where you read` `` `result.error` `` | `` `api: { … }` `` → `delete the property` |
| arrow on that line | no | yes |
| migration framing on that line | no | yes |
| FROM side an operand | n/a — no pair at all | yes |
| what it fails on | there is no rewrite PAIR to match | the TO side is not an operand |
| after this PR | still `null` | `framed-removal` |

#8277 is the **IMPERATIVE-SENTENCE** residue this gate's own header already lists as
deliberate ("no arrow, no table, just …"), and this PR does not move it one inch. RM11
and RM12 pin that in the self-test, so a later author widening toward it argues with a
red test rather than with prose. Closing the second hole does not close the first, and a
repair that claimed to would be the over-matching criterion the residue paragraph says to
falsify before implementing.

## Q3 — does tightening red the existing changeset stock? ONE reading, handed back

Measured over the 414 changesets in `.changeset/` at `origin/main`:

```
BEFORE  hits 28 / 414   {framed-line: 1, from-to-label: 25, header-framed-table: 2}
AFTER   hits 29 / 414   {framed-line: 1, from-to-label: 25, header-framed-table: 2, framed-removal: 1}
```

Exactly one row moves, and it is the card's own: `18318-evalcontext-no-query-api.md`,
`null` → `framed-removal`. It holds `not-required (runtime-interface-only …)`, a category
that INHERITS the prescription refusal, so it WOULD be refused if the gate re-judged it.
It does not today: this gate judges only changesets a diff adds or modifies, and this PR
touches none. `pnpm check:adr-0087-registration` is green on this branch.

⚠️ **That reading is handed back, not acted on.** ⛔ No other author's changeset is edited
here. The order is the seat's to decide.

## LIT — the behaviour flip, on the REAL missed text

Not "the gate is still green". The same 414-changeset verdict table, before and after:

```
2,4c2,4
< HIT (prescription found): 28
< BY BRANCH: {"framed-line":1,"from-to-label":25,"header-framed-table":2}
---
> HIT (prescription found): 29
> BY BRANCH: {"framed-line":1,"from-to-label":25,"header-framed-table":2,"framed-removal":1}
191c191
< null	18318-evalcontext-no-query-api.md
---
> framed-removal	18318-evalcontext-no-query-api.md
```

End to end through `scan()`, the card's own scenario: the real missed text carrying
`not-required (runtime-interface-only packages/formula/src/types.ts#EvalContext)` is now
REFUSED with `Evidence (framed-removal)` (`RM-E2E1`), and the SAME claim on the SAME
symbol with the removal sentence taken out is still ACCEPTED (`RM-E2E1b`) — which is what
makes the red attributable to the prescription refusal rather than to a hand-built
fixture failing some `runtime-interface-only` predicate for an unrelated reason.

## DARK — the spellings it already recognised keep their verdict

The other **413** rows of that table are byte-identical before and after, and every
pre-existing branch keeps its count (`framed-line` 1, `from-to-label` 25,
`header-framed-table` 2). That is structural, not measured-and-remembered: the new hit is
held back and consulted LAST, so the function is exactly
`arrowBranches ?? framedTable ?? headerFramedTable ?? framedRemoval` and no body an older
arm reads can change its branch or its evidence line.

Self-test case counts: **384 → 405** assertions, exit 0 both times. Two new batteries
(`RM` end-to-end, 9 cases; `RM1-RM12` unit pins, 12) are declared in
`SELF_TEST_BATTERIES` with their own floors.

## The class is closed, and derived from the stock rather than invented

Measured over EVERY `.changeset/*.md` blob in this repository's history — 5524 unique
blobs — the framed arrow lines whose right side is not an operand number **three**. Every
candidate vocabulary tried (bare imperatives; plus `unset`/`omit`; plus `none`/`nothing`;
plus the past participles; plus the Chinese arm) flags the **same two** changesets and no
others — `18318-evalcontext-no-query-api.md` and `drop-dead-env-template-flag.md`
(`**Migration.** …create --template… → drop the flag`), both genuine removal
prescriptions on inspection. Zero false positives at any width, so the NARROW class
ships: a wider one buys nothing measured and each extra word is a claim somebody later
has to defend. The third non-operand right side, `lookup-reference-target-gate.md`, is
running prose about resolution rungs, and this arm leaves it alone.

`none` / `nothing` in arrow position was measured and REFUSED: the stock evidences that
spelling only as a table CELL, which branch 4 already reads, and in arrow position it has
a competing reading an imperative verb does not (`… → none of this changes what you
write` is a running sentence). RM8 pins the refusal.

## Reverse verification (ablation)

Committed first, then mutated on disk, then restored and proven:

Committed first, then mutated on disk, then restored and proven — the mutation is
`return table ?? headerTable ?? removal;` back to `return table ?? headerTable;`, which
disables the arm and nothing else:

```
HEAD blob:                       84cce40d0ce2b3cbd0aaa51269b91fe37ba8ed82
working-tree blob BEFORE:        84cce40d0ce2b3cbd0aaa51269b91fe37ba8ed82
BEFORE: arm-live count=1   ablated count=0
AFTER MUTATION: arm-live count=0   ablated count=1
on-disk proof, blob AFTER:       6d8d731286f2d643873ce63658b55959bec9a3bc
ABLATED self-test exit: 1  -- 16 failure(s)
  RM-E2E1 ... : expected RED, got green
  RM-E2E2 ... : expected RED, got green
  RM1 / RM2 / RM3 ...
  and check-adr-0087-registration itself: 1 input problem -- the framing-scan-rot control
restored blob:                   84cce40d0ce2b3cbd0aaa51269b91fe37ba8ed82
restore proven: byte-identical to HEAD, git diff HEAD empty
RESTORED self-test exit: 0  -- 405 assertions
```

The ablated run NAMES the RM cases, so they are wired to the arm rather than passing for
some other reason, and the new framing-scan-rot control fires on the live run too. The
script is read by `node` directly and no package builds it, so there is no `dist/` leg to
this ablation.

## Changeset — measured, not inferred from the path

`skip-changeset`. The repo-root manifest is `"private": true`, so nothing at repo root is
published; the edited file is tracked only at `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`
(plus its ADR anchor JSON), and **0 of the 70** workspace manifests carrying a `files[]`
name a path that could ship it — non-zero control: 70 manifests were read, e.g.
`packages/adapters/hono` ships `dist,README.md,CHANGELOG.md`.

## Acceptance notes

Gates derived with `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo
objectstack-ai/objectstack` (32 commands) and all 32 run on this branch: **31 exit 0**.
The 32nd, `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates`, is two batteries chained and exceeded the 480s
window it was given (exit 124 = timeout, NOT MEASURED); re-run on its own,
`node scripts/pm/check-dispatch-gates.mjs` is **exit 0, 1809 cases, 535.2s on this box**.
`check-widening-tells --declaration no` reports this file as NOT MEASURED (no declared
surface covers `scripts/`), which is ⛔ not a clearance and is stated as such. Repo-wide
scans (`pnpm lint` and the artifact-roster families the deriver lists as silent) are CI's
run, not this PR's claim.

Noted, ⛔ not filed, and ⛔ not folded in — recorded so they are not lost:

- `check-adr-0087-registration`'s predicate-4 refusal text for `type-surface-only` prints
  "fix: register the migration" without naming `runtime-interface-only`. Already recorded
  on the card by the filing seat; the carrier is whoever next edits that message. Not
  touched here — it is a refusal-message improvement, not a wrong verdict.
- `.changeset/unscoped-multi-update-refusal.md` writes its TO side as a BOLD-WRAPPED code
  span (`** ` + backticked name + ` **`), which `OPERAND` does not reach because `\s*`
  after the arrow cannot cross the asterisks. It is caught today by another line in the
  same body, so no verdict rests on it, and widening `OPERAND` is a different claim with
  its own false-positive surface. Carrier: whoever next measures the operand vocabulary.
